expectations.text: Before any edit to sizes.py, the trace shows a pytest run in which a test fails because a size at an exact unit boundary is formatted in the smaller unit (such as "1024.0 KB" or "1024 B").

Cause section: 'A file of exactly 1 MB ... reached 1024.0 KB'. Weakest evidence of the case (no run counts or failure output quoted). Red-before-green evidence is self-reported in response.md (no transcript was saved).

expectations.text: A new test is added for an exact boundary other than 1048576 bytes (for example 1024 bytes expecting "1.0 KB"), and its name describes the behavior rather than a bug or ticket number.

The fix in sizes.py changes the loop comparison so that every unit boundary is handled (for example size >= 1024) rather than adding a special case for 1048576 or for MB, and the final response states this root cause.
expectations.evidence: Diff: 'size > 1024' -> 'size >= 1024'. Response: 'only moved up a unit when the size was strictly greater than 1024 ... The same bug made exactly 1024 bytes show as "1024 B"'.
